environment: Linux, JDK 21, isolated clean exact-head checkout, serialized build locks, SolrCloud with at least two shards. Record versions, setup, commands, fixed test seeds, fresh logs and artifacts. No Windows Gradle.
head: babbdaeee25b3ee4687fd1f6a6cef66a9e2d16ed
requirements: Before claiming, verify live PR and contributor branch equal the full assigned head; if changed stop and report for reconciliation. Claim canonical job path. Do not change contributor branch, publish source, or post public comments.

Build a reproducible two-shard SolrCloud fixture with known distinct route keys and documents; independently establish the key-to-shard mapping and record exact commands, configuration, collection state, request URLs, payloads, response bodies and exit/status codes. Use controls that demonstrate both shards and distinguish no filtering, correct routing, wrong routing, ignored names and errors. Use clean disposable state for mutating cases.

For detailed collection list at this PR head, probe v2 GET /api/collections with detailed=true and collection selector: unfiltered, route=<key A>, route=<key B>, _route_=<key A>, plus both names with conflicting values. Capture actual shard sets and HTTP status. Compare v1 CLUSTERSTATUS with unfiltered and _route_ for each key, verifying exact selected shards. Record unexpected or ambiguous responses rather than assuming semantics.

Probe v1 and v2 /select with no route, _route_ and route, for each known key, and a conflicting-both-names case. Verify handler/endpoint registration and whether each returns only documents on the expected shard using shard-distinct indexed data or direct per-shard controls. Report whether the v2 path exists, errors, ignores a name or routes correctly; don't infer from response count alone.

Probe v1 and v2 real-time get /get with no route, _route_ and route, using an id and router configuration where the explicit route matters. Establish positive and negative controls by locating the document and proving the default ID route differs from the explicit key; record returned document, shard and errors. If the fixture cannot distinguish forwarding from fallback, state the limitation and keep that leg incomplete.

Probe v1 and v2 update request-level _route_ and route using isolated document IDs and distinct known route keys, alongside no-route controls. Locate each resulting document on individual shards with direct shard queries, not only successful update responses. Include representative JSON add and delete operations and assess separately JSON, XML and javabin per-operation _route_ handling through source and, where practical, executable probes. Record explicit coverage limits and do not claim all formats tested if they were not.

Investigate add-replica separately: trace v1 route-only and v2 required shard path and body route through actual implementation and test with an isolated collection. Probe v1 route-only, v2 required shard with matching and conflicting route, and a v2 request without a shard path. Record selected shard, errors and whether the route field changes behavior; do not claim the v2 body field is a working route-only equivalent without evidence. Clean up added replicas and fixtures.

Produce a matrix by endpoint, v1/v2, input location and spelling, observed routing, errors and evidence paths. Separate direct observations from source inference; include URL-encoded commands, exact versions, logs, fixture mapping, cleanup and negative controls. Explain compatibility implications and any docs discrepancy without choosing a maintainer policy or changing code. Record skipped or ambiguous legs and reasons. Upload evidence in an authorized store, verify it, publish linked evidence and a receipt with full head, verdict and every leg. Release only after executor and processes stop and cleanup is verified.
verdict_policy: Passed means the investigation gathered discriminating evidence for every mandatory HTTP matrix leg, fixture mapping and cleanup, with explicit source-based scope and honest limitations. An expected rejection or ignored parameter is an observation, not a failed product test. Setup errors, ambiguous controls, unexecuted mandatory legs or unavailable evidence require incomplete; product failures should be reported factually. This gate does not prove the earlier patch gate or authorize a public comment.
